proposed_fix.description: Confirm network-level packet loss affecting the ts-route-service pod/node, then mitigate by gated, reversible moves such as rescheduling the pod, while checking interface errors and conntrack before any node change.
steps: Check the node hosting ts-route-service for interface TX/RX errors, drops, and retransmits (e.g. node_network_transmit_errs_total, netstat/ip -s link) to confirm loss at the node level.
Check the node's conntrack usage (nf_conntrack_count vs nf_conntrack_max) to see whether table exhaustion could be causing drops.
Inspect ts-route-service socket growth (socket z=11.8) and connection states to see whether connections are piling up or stalling.
Compare latency on ts-route-service replicas/pods on different nodes to determine whether the problem is node-local.
If the problem is node-local, with approval, cordon the node and delete/reschedule the ts-route-service pod onto a healthy node, one replica at a time.
If conntrack is near its limit, with approval, raise the limit on the node as a temporary change, noting the previous value.
Watch ts-route-service latency-50/90 and the upstream ts-travel-service / ts-admin-travel-service latencies for recovery after each step.
preconditions: Confirm node-level evidence (interface errors/drops or conntrack pressure) exists before touching the node; current telemetry shows latency and socket deviation only, not direct transmit errors.
Verify other replicas or capacity exist so rescheduling ts-route-service does not cause an outage.
Record current conntrack limit and pod placement before changes.
Obtain human approval for each mutating step.
proposed_fix.rollback: Uncordon the node, restore the previous conntrack limit value, and, if the new placement is worse, reschedule the pod back or scale replicas to the prior configuration.
